title.narrative: OECS Data for Decision Making (DDM) Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS) Data for Decision Making Project for Grenada, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Organization of Eastern Caribbean States Commission is to improve the capacity of Participating Eastern Caribbean countries to: (i) produce and publicly disseminate statistical data for country and regional level analytics; and (ii) provide immediate and effective response to an eligible emergency. The project comprises of five components. The first component, statistical modernization and capacity building will support the modernization of the National Statistical System (NSS). It consists of following sub-components: (i) national statistical office development; (ii) strengthening the NSS; (iii) information technologies for statistics; and (iv) promoting data access and use. The second component, data collection, analysis, and dissemination will support the production of core data products central to the statistical system and some supplemental data to fill other key data gaps identified by participating countries. It consists of following sub-components: (i) core data; and (ii) supplemental data. The third component, OECS regional integration contributes to the OECSC's mandate for regional integration and strengthening the regional statistical system. It consists of following sub-components: (i) OECS regional data governance council; (ii) data innovation for small island developing states; (iii) regional technical assistance and capacity building; and (iv) regional data aggregation, analysis, and dissemination. The fourth component, project implementation will support project implementation in each country and at the OECSC. The fifth component, contingency emergency response component (CERC) zero-cost component aims to provide immediate surge funding in an eligible national emergency.

To improve the capacity of Participating Eastern Caribbean Countries to (i) produce and publicly disseminate statistical data for country and regional level analytics; and (ii) provide immediate and effective response to an Eligible Emergency.

condition.narrative: Grenada and OECS Commission:Pursuant to the Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.1(d), the Recipient shall develop andadopt a Project Operational Manual ("POM"), satisfactory to the Association, no later than thirty (30) days as of the EffectiveDate.

Grenada and Saint Lucia:Pursuant to the Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.C, the Recipient shall disclose and makeavailable to the public through official portals the statistics and Microdata, including census and survey reports and keydevelopment indicators, produced through the data collection operations conducted as part of the Project, in a manner consistentwith the POM, including (i) the Statistical Disclosure Calendar; and (ii) the applicable Personal Data protocols.

Grenada, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, and OECS Commission:The Recipient shall carry out the Project inaccordance with the Implementation Arrangements set out in Section I, Schedule 2 of the Financing Agreement.

OECS Commission:Pursuant to the Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.C.1, the Recipient shall develop a Sub-Grants Manual,in a manner and with contents acceptable to the Association, including, inter alia: (a) detailed arrangements and procedures inrelation to the Experiments, including the eligibility criteria, procedures, guidelines and templates for the selection, approval,administration and supervision of Experiments; (b) terms and conditions for the provision of Sub-Grants, including eligibilitycriteria, application, appraisal, approval and disbursement procedures; and; (c) an Implementation Agreement template.

Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Pursuant to the Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.1(d), theRecipient shall develop and adopt a POM, satisfactory to the Association, no later than forty-five (45) days as of the EffectiveDate.

Saint Vincent and the Grenadines:Pursuant to the Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.C, the Recipient shall disclose andmake available to the public through official portals the statistics and Microdata, including census and survey reports and keydevelopment indicators, produced through the data collection operations conducted as part of the Project, in a manner consistentwith (a) the POM, including (i) the Statistical Disclosure Calendar; and (ii) the applicable Personal Data protocols; and (b) anyapplicable legislation; provided that in the event of any contradiction or inconsistency between (a) and (b) regarding PersonalData, the higher protection standard would apply.

title.narrative: Number of participants trained via OECS regional training programs

comment.narrative: Current status: A total of 145 persons participated in the trainings listed under IRI 15. Adjustments required: The mission agreed not to include additional training activities under the revised project. Indicator to be dropped.

title.narrative: Number of participants trained via OECS regional training programs

comment.narrative: To date, 145 people have been trained in OECSC regional training programs supported by the project. There is no certification via OECS Academy yet.

title.narrative: Data privacy policy published online (Share of participating countries)

comment.narrative:
Current status: GRD: 0, LCA: 0, VCT: 0.
Adjustments required: All countries already have online statements indicating that the statistical office operates in line with data privacy requirements as per the national Statistical Act. None of the countries are currently implementing further activities to develop a data privacy policy and there is no avenue to achieve this target under the Project. Indicator to be dropped.

title.narrative: Data privacy policy published online (Share of participating countries)

comment.narrative: None of the countries have published a data privacy policy as of yet. While achievement of this target is delayed, it is deemed possible to achieve it by project closing by all three countries. At the time of the mid-term missions, the timeline for this was expected to be communicated by the PIUs by: • GRD: August 2025 • LCA: September 2025 • VCT: July 2025 (missed)

title.narrative: Number of countries that produce data according to published statistical release calendars

comment.narrative: As of yet, none of the countries publish data according to predetermined release calendars. All three countries are revising their Statistical Disclosure Calendar, which are an annex to the POM, to update release dates. Thereafter, they will need to publish a statistical release calendar on the respective CSO websites. At the time of the mid-term missions, the agreed expected dates for revising their Statistical Disclosure Calendar: • GRD: November 2025 • LCA: November 2025 • VCT: July 2025 (missed) Based on past experience and challenges in keeping with preestablished timelines and setting up procedures for data publication, even after the submission of new release calendars it is not a given that countries will publish data according to these calendars.

title.narrative: Number of countries that produce data according to published statistical release calendars

comment.narrative:
Current status: GRD: 0, LCA: 0, VCT: 0.
Adjustments required: None of the countries are currently implementing activities to meet this target and there is no avenue to achieve this target under the Project. Indicator to be dropped.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries' satisfaction (%) with the implementation of the Communication Strategy

comment.narrative:
Current status: GRD: 0, LCA: 0, VCT: 0.
Adjustments required: None of the countries have measured beneficiary satisfaction to date. A strategy to do so is lacking and proves too complicated to develop. The countries agree to change the indicator as follows: “Share of countries that have developed a communication strategy and are implementing this strategy through dedicated human resources.” The World Bank Task Team is still coordinating internally to determine if this indicator is appropriate and can be approved. New baseline: 0. New end-target: 1.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries' satisfaction (%) with the implementation of the Communication Strategy

comment.narrative: None of the entities is measuring this corporate citizen engagement indicator, which should measure beneficiary satisfaction with the design and implementation of the communication strategy and Stakeholder Engagement Plan. For this, annual beneficiary satisfaction surveys will need to be carried out. The OECS Commission was to develop the content of the survey and detailed mechanism for collecting this data in coordination with participant countries before the end of the first year of implementation. During the MTR it was agreed that the WB Social Specialist would work with all PIUs to clarify the requirements for this indicator so that it can be measured going forward.

title.narrative: Number of recent surveys with tabulations of key indicators online

comment.narrative:
Current status: GRD: 0, LCA: 0, VCT: 0.
Adjustments required: Expand indicator definition to include censuses conducted under the Project and adjust target. Adjust end-target to 12, reflecting the continued ambition to implement the following four data collection activities in each participating country: Population and housing census (completed in all three countries), Census of Agriculture and Fisheries, Labor Force Survey, and Survey of Living Conditions / Household Budget Survey.

title.narrative: Number of RDGC approved methodological guidance notes published online

comment.narrative: Current status: None Adjustments required: Target to be revised downwards. Concrete target still to be determined.

title.narrative: Number of data innovation experiments, including accompanying report of findings

comment.narrative: Current status: Reports for two experiments have submitted to the World Bank Task Team. Reports still need to be published online in accordance with the Project Operations Manual. Adjustments required: The mission agreed not to implement any additional data innovation experiments under the revised project. Indicator to be dropped.

title.narrative: NSDS document submitted for adoption (Share of participating countries)

comment.narrative: Expected to be completed soon. At the time of the MTR missions, the countries indicated the following expected timelines: - GRD: Submission to Cabinet by July 2025 (status unclear) - LCA: Complete draft by October 2025 and submission to Cabinet in November 2025. - VCT: Submission to Cabinet by July 2025 (delayed)

title.narrative: Number of RDGC approved methodological guidance notes published online

comment.narrative: No methodological guidance notes have been produced or published to date. With 2 years remaining under the project, a significant effort is needed to achieve progress against this IRI.

title.narrative: Number of recent surveys with tabulations of key indicators online

comment.narrative:
Partly due to the delays in data collection activities and need for additional technical assistance to produce outputs, none of the countries has produced tabulations of key indicators of surveys conducted under the Project. It is unclear whether the targets for this indicator were set in line with its definition. If only surveys are considered, the target is unlikely to be met. However, considering both surveys and censuses conducted under the Project, achieving the target is still considered possible.
Adjustments needed: Expand definition to include censuses conducted under the Project.

title.narrative: Number of data innovation experiments, including accompanying report of findings

comment.narrative: Two data innovation experiments have been initiated. These explore: i) use of administrative data in Grenada; and ii) use of drone imagery in Saint Lucia. Considering capacity constraints, no other experiments in the original form will be prepared. Coordination on the appropriate course of action on this indicator is needed once there is clarity on the implementation plan for the remaining lifetime of the Project and need for restructuring.

title.narrative: Average number of household survey datasets per Participating Eastern Caribbean country accessible via the OECS Regional Microdata Catalog

comment.narrative:
Current status: GRD: 0, LCA: 2, VCT: 0. While the OECS Regional Microdata Catalog is now online, it neither contains microdata produced under the Project (as those are not yet anonymized and cleared for release), nor surveys or censuses documented recently as the result of a training financed under Component 3. The Catalog does contain microdata for two older Saint Lucia surveys: the 2010 Enterprise Survey and the 2012 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey.
Adjustments required: For the restructuring, the proposal is to broaden the definition of this indicator to formally count business and enterprise surveys. The original target will remain unchanged. Based on extensive coordination between the 4 PIUs, the 3 Statistical Offices, and the World Bank team, the following country-level targets were established: GRD: 12, LCA: 16, VCT: 4.

title.narrative: Average number of household survey datasets per Participating Eastern Caribbean country accessible via the OECS Regional Microdata Catalog

comment.narrative: While the OECS Regional Microdata Catalog is now online, it neither contains microdata produced under the Project (as those are not yet anonymized and cleared for release), nor surveys or censuses documented. recently as the result of a training financed under Component 3. According to the WB task team's calculations, the current values for the three countries are as follows: GRD: 0, LCA: 2, VCT: 0. The OECS Commission is preparing to recruit a consultant to determine the procedures for microdata release. In addition, a consultancy needs to be commissioned to provide technical assistance in anonymizing the data. Clarity on the scope for this consultancy is expected by end-October 2025.

title.narrative: Number of OECS regional publications featuring harmonized statistics across Participating Eastern Caribbean countries.

comment.narrative:
Current status: One thematic report on education has been published on the OECS DDM website: https://oecs.int/en/our-work/knowledge/library/projects/oecs-data-for-decision-making. This report, however, is not based on data collected by Participating Countries under the Project.
Adjustments required: None, this target is on track to be achieved. ToRs for two additional reports on elderly and youth populations in the OECS based on PHC data collected by the countries under the Project are in advanced stages. An additional ToR will be developed for a report on migration, also based on the PHC data. PIUs confirmed that the PHC data can be shared with the consultants for the purpose of preparing these reports.

title.narrative: Number of OECS regional publications featuring harmonized statistics across Participating Eastern Caribbean countries.

comment.narrative:
One thematic report on education has been published on the OECS DDM website: https://oecs.int/en/our-work/knowledge/library/projects/oecs-data-for-decision-making. This report, however, is not based on data collected by Participating Countries under the Project.
Publication of additional reports is pending the release of new data by the NSOs. Two reports are being planned based on the Population and Housing Census recently completed in all three countries. The first report will focus on housing stocks. The topic of the second report will be determined in July, when all three countries are expected to have completed the PHC data processing. It is unclear whether reports on other surveys and censuses conducted under the Project can be completed before the project closing date, given the delays in the start of these.

title.narrative: Number of energy-efficient computing systems provided to the statistical offices

comment.narrative:
Country values: GRD: 35, LCA: 26, VCT: 53.
Plans for further procurement: - GRD: The remaining equipment to be procured before the end of the Project is expected to be clear by end-August 2025 - LCA: The remaining equipment to be procured before the end of the Project is expected to be clear by end-August 2025 - VCT: No further procurement foreseen
Adjustments needed: It is unclear whether the targets for this indicator were set in line with its definition. The indicator measures the number of desktop computers and laptops provided by the project that are energy-efficient. Statistical offices, however, also procured tablets under the Project (GRD 310, LCA 120, VCT 400). If these would be considered, assuming they are energy-efficient, the target would have been exceeded by a considerable margin. The WB will review the need for adjustments in definition and/or targets with the PIUs.

title.narrative: Number of regionally harmonized methods for data collection and analysis published by the RDGC.

comment.narrative:
The RDGC adopted two harmonized questionnaires: • Labor Force Survey • Survey of Living Conditions / Household Budget Survey (documentation not yet online)
There were some delays in developing harmonized methods under the RDGC as its set-up took some time and this newly established body needed some onboarding time. Another challenge has been that recruited support staff (statistician) did not fully fulfill the intended on supporting the planning and implementation of the development of such methods. There is now a need to identify additional harmonized methods that would be helpful for NSOs in meeting their commitments under the project (notably anonymization of microdata) and plan for implementation.
Adjustments needed: There is a need to determine and refine what outputs will be considered here in addition to harmonized questionnaires.

title.narrative: Number of OECS annual statistical bulletins published

comment.narrative: Two bulletins were published on the OECS DDM Project website to date, with a thematic focus on the youth and elderly population in the OECS countries. The published bulletins do, however, not meet the standards and objectives envisioned at project appraisal. Meeting this target is still feasible in the remaining timeline, but will require a change in approach to prepare bulletins of higher analytical quality and policy relevance. The latter will require recruitment of additional support services (following the recommendation for bundled procurement). Alternatively, a potential for dropping this activity may have to be explored.

title.narrative: Customized Statistical Performance Indicator, average value for Participating Eastern Caribbean countries.

comment.narrative:
Current status: There has been limited progress against this results indicator in part due to delays in documenting recent censuses and surveys in the OECS Microdata Catalogue. Moreover, original targets for this indicator can no longer be achieved due to downward revisions in the number of data collection activities to be implemented under the Project.
Adjustments required: In addition to the challenges outlined above, the indicator is too complex for the Project to monitor. The following, simplified indicator is considered for the restructuring: “Number of targeted household surveys conducted using RDGC-approved harmonized survey instruments”. The baseline for this is 1, as Grenada already carried out a labor force survey based on the RDGC-approved harmonized instrument. The end-target is 6, as every country still intends to administer both a labor force survey and a survey of living conditions / household budget survey.

title.narrative: Customized Statistical Performance Indicator, average value for Participating Eastern Caribbean countries.

comment.narrative:
Progress on the data sources pillar of the cSPI is hampered by delays in documenting recent censuses and surveys in the OECS Microdata Catalogue. While the finalization of PHCs and surveys and the publication of the microdata will contribute to progress, the overall target can no longer be achieved before the closing of the Project. For this to happen, Saint Lucia and Grenada needed to conduct two rounds of the SLCHBS and have the data of the second round available before June 2027 to produce comparable poverty headcounts at the International Poverty Line. This is not feasible anymore.
Adjustments needed: - The current baseline value is no longer accurate and will need to be recalculated to ensure that the same source is used for data sources pillar for all countries, and account for ex-post revision of Grenada's data infrastructure score. - The end target and June 2026 intermediate target will have to be adjusted based on changes in project design agreed during MTR.

title.narrative: Number of UNSD Minimum List gender indicators published

comment.narrative:
Current status: GRD: 0, LCA: 0, VCT: 0.
Adjustments required: None of the statistical offices currently have a dedicated place to publish UNSD Minimum List gender indicators. Moreover, the countries cannot currently provide an overview of the UNSD Minimum List Gender indicators that can be generated with available data or data to be collected under the Project. The proposal is to replace this indicator with one regional report focused on gender. The regional report will draw on the PHC data and any other data sources generated under the Project (potentially LFS or SLC/HBS) that are available at the time of initiating the activity. The report will compile the UNSD Minimum List Gender indicators to the maximum extent possible, and generate recommendations on expanding that list in the future. New baseline: 0. New end-target: 1, under Component 3.
